title: `teploy sandbox exec --json` (rev 23, sandbox-v1): how the command ended, with its output captured instead of streamed. The output is had from the engine byte for byte (the engine is asked for base64 when it is a release that speaks it); stdout and stderr are it as text, and a stream holding bytes that are not valid UTF-8 is given as base64 beside it. Printed only once the engine has taken the command (it answered 200): an exec it refused prints the error envelope on stderr alone. It is printed when the command exits nonzero too: teploy then exits with the command's own status (255 for a failure of teploy's own) and the error envelope on stderr is code `command-failed`.

server.description: The server as the command was given it (--host).

host.description: The SSH host the server resolved to.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status; -1 when the sandbox itself could not run the command (stderr says why); null when the stream ended before the command's exit was known, in which case whether it finished is unknown.

timed_out.description: The command's own timeout ended it.

stdout.description: The command's standard output, at most 1 MiB. Text: each byte that is not valid UTF-8 is U+FFFD, and stdout_base64 then holds the stream itself.

stderr.description: The command's standard error, at most 1 MiB. Text: each byte that is not valid UTF-8 is U+FFFD, and stderr_base64 then holds the stream itself.

stdout_base64.description: Only when stdout holds bytes that are not valid UTF-8: the stream byte for byte, in base64 (at most 1 MiB decoded). Absent means stdout is already byte for byte.

stderr_base64.description: Only when stderr holds bytes that are not valid UTF-8: the stream byte for byte, in base64 (at most 1 MiB decoded). Absent means stderr is already byte for byte.

truncated.description: A stream was longer than the capture and was cut.
